submission.name: Campus Watchtower
submission.tagline: Use a camera view and Gemini to flag possible campus facility incidents for review.
submission.inspiration: A maintenance or safety issue can be easy to miss when it is only reported after someone walks away. We wanted to see whether a small camera-based prototype could help campus operations staff notice possible incidents sooner.
submission.what_it_does: Campus Watchtower analyzes a selected camera image or short feed sample with Gemini and labels possible issues such as smoke, blocked access, or an unusual crowd. It shows the location on a map and offers a suggested route to inspect the area. The output is a review prompt for staff, not an automatic emergency dispatch.
submission.how_we_built_it: We used Next.js for the dashboard and API, MongoDB for incident records, and Gemini for image and text analysis. A separate Python process checks the configured camera sample and posts candidate events, which the dashboard maps and turns into an inspection suggestion.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: Working with low-quality or changing camera views made incident labels inconsistent, so results still need human review. The prototype runs through the demo flow, though it has only been exercised with a small set of configured feeds and does not cover a broad live camera network.
submission.accomplishments: We connected image analysis, an incident list, and mapped inspection routes into one usable prototype. We also made the uncertainty visible by presenting detections as candidates to verify.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned that image quality and camera placement shape what a model can reasonably identify. Building around hardware feeds also made us think about timing, retries, and how to keep a camera failure from looking like an all-clear.
submission.whats_next: We would test against more varied camera conditions and add better feed health reporting. We would also make route suggestions account for access restrictions and staff availability.
